# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (ranking and track from your partner's words, 2026-11-06). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with four package scaffolds (root `pyproject.toml`). Azure services per the ADR (Proposed, 2026-10-05).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a configured range, downloaded and kept (R1) | A | 1 | Requests: about 2 per quarter (listing + `master.idx`), so a 120-quarter range uses under a minute of budget at 3 req/s (spec §4.8). Bytes: measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs (R2) | A | 2 | About 1 file per business day, roughly 250 a year; negligible request budget |
| O3 | Ingested indexes turned into one canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet (R3) | A | 3 | Rows, elapsed time and peak memory per quarter: measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipeline runs on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor (R4) | A | 4 | Azure spend: measured by Stage 6's smoke test. Spec §4.8 leaves resource sizes open, so there is no estimate before that |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation share one downloader, parser and publisher (R5) | A | 5 | Not material |
| O6 | Original bytes kept; a parser change reprocesses them with no new download (R6) | A | 6 | Storage is the raw bytes plus one observation copy per parser version; measured by Stage 1 and Stage 2 |
| O7 | The quarterly baseline is re-checked periodically for corrections (R7) | A | 7 | Each weekly run re-downloads every supported quarter, so roughly the O1 bytes each week; measured by Stage 1 |
| O8 | All SEC traffic goes through one downloader and one request budget (R8) | A | 8 | Not material |
| O9 | Readers get each quarter through a versioned manifest and one active pointer (R9) | A | 9 | Storage: one retained generation per publication; retention is set at deployment (spec §4.8) |
| O10 | Records leave a closed quarter only with approval tied to the source hash (R10) | A | 10 | Operator time per approval: measured by the first real reconciliation in Stage 8 |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target are reviewed configuration (R11) | A | 11 | Not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression). One track: every outcome serves one catalog, and each later outcome builds on the earlier ones.

## Open questions

1. **Spec and ADR are PROPOSED.** Spec §7 step 1 makes acceptance of both the first step. Stages 1–5 do not depend on Azure. Acceptance gates Stage 6 at the latest. Accept before Stage 1, or before Stage 6?
2. **Package placement.** Spec §4.9 puts all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repo also scaffolds `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, and the root script points to a `sec_edgar` module that does not exist. Settle this in Stage 1's brainstorming, or answer it here first.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Quarterly baseline on real data (core)
      Objective: Download a configured range of archived quarterly master indexes from the SEC and turn them into canonical Parquet rows, running locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing; only the uv workspace scaffold
      Produces: a backfill command over an inclusive quarter range that keeps original bytes with SHA-256 and writes rows in the `sec-index-v1` contract (spec §4.5); specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: at least one real archived quarter is fetched with an identifying User-Agent at ≤3 req/s, and its original bytes are kept with their hash. O3: that quarter's rows are in Parquet and pass the row contract; malformed rows are refused, never dropped. Measured cost of the real run, in the findings file: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and request rate.
      Leaves out: source manifest, checkpoints and replay → Stage 2; daily indexes and the shared request lease → Stage 3; versioned generations and the active pointer → Stage 4; reconciliation and withdrawals → Stage 5; Azure services → Stage 6; typed config validation, golden fixtures across the full range, alerts and runbooks → Stage 7; production backfill → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Durable source state and replay
      Objective: Record source, snapshot, processing and attempt state so a failed run resumes per source file and a parser change reprocesses kept bytes.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's backfill command and kept raw bytes
      Produces: spec §4.5 Source, Snapshot, Workset binding, Processing and Attempt records behind a storage interface; immutable worksets; observation output keyed by snapshot, parser and schema
      Exit: O6: a parser-version bump rebuilds observation output from raw storage with SEC access disabled. A backfill killed mid-range resumes without refetching completed sources. Repeated runs over the same inputs and versions add no logical rows.
      Leaves out: Quarter publication and Withdrawal approval records → Stages 4 and 5; Table Storage and ADLS backing → Stage 6
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Daily ingestion under one request budget
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries, with every SEC request going through one leased downloader.
      Outcomes: O2, O8
      Consumes: Stage 2's source manifest and worksets
      Produces: daily discovery and collection from a handoff date; one downloader with lease, retries and spec §5 access outcomes, used by backfill too
      Exit: O2: in CI, a missed run and a multi-quarter outage catch up; a failed listing does not advance the boundary; a valid empty listing reports `no_new_sources`; overlap with the baseline deduplicates. O8: in CI, concurrent backfill and daily collectors never issue overlapping requests, retries count toward the budget, and a 403 halts access.
      Leaves out: the lease on real Azure Storage → Stage 6; scheduled triggers → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation that readers reach through one conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's observation output; Stage 3's daily observations
      Produces: generation-addressed output with `manifest.json` and `changes.parquet`; an active pointer with a conditional-write version; spec §4.4 identity and open-quarter precedence
      Exit: O9: crashes injected before files finish, before the pointer update and after it leave readers seeing only complete generations. Competing publishers cannot lose an update. Reads resolve through the pointer, never by globbing.
      Leaves out: the closed-quarter withdrawal gate → Stage 5; the pointer on Table Storage → Stage 6; the rollback runbook → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish additions and updates, and hold any key removal for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10, O5
      Consumes: Stages 2–4
      Produces: a reconcile command; withdrawal approval records; the `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7: on corrected fixtures, a changed snapshot publishes additions and field updates with a change report, and an unchanged hash skips transformation. O10: a closed-quarter snapshot that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its exact hash and candidate generation. Open-quarter absence and HTTP failures never withdraw, and stale daily replay cannot bring back a withdrawn key. O5: backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation differ only in source selection and call the same downloader, parser and publisher.
      Leaves out: the approval runbook → Stage 7; real reconciliation runs and approvals → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure platform
      Objective: Run the shared worker as Container Apps Jobs orchestrated by ADF, backed by ADLS, Table Storage and Log Analytics, in an isolated environment.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–5's commands and storage interfaces; an accepted ADR (Open question 1)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure, managed identities, a pinned image digest, and ADF pipelines with triggers disabled; integration tests
      Exit: O4: isolated-environment integration tests pass for job start and poll (including an ambiguous start), lease coordination, the conditional pointer update and log delivery. A live smoke test of one archived quarter and one daily index records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest, request rate and Azure spend. Replay from raw storage with SEC access disabled changes nothing.
      Leaves out: production triggers → Stage 8; alerts and runbooks → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Configuration, observability and runbooks
      Objective: Make spec §4.8's defaults a validated, reviewed configuration, and give operators reports, alerts and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 6's isolated environment
      Produces: typed configuration validated before I/O; run reports and alerts (spec §4.7); runbooks (spec §8); golden fixtures for every historical format in the chosen backfill range
      Exit: O11: each spec §5 configuration error is refused before any external I/O, including a rate at or above the published ceiling. Each spec §4.7 alert fires in the isolated environment. The approval and rollback runbooks are rehearsed on corrected fixtures. The golden fixtures pass for the configured range.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 8: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill, catch daily ingestion up from the handoff, reconcile once, then enable the triggers and observe scheduled runs (spec §7 Phase 2).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7
      Consumes: Stages 6–7
      Produces: active generations for every requested quarter; enabled daily and weekly triggers; a release record
      Exit: O1: every requested quarter is published, or the incomplete range is recorded, with no silent gaps. O2: the daily trigger is enabled after the catch-up is accepted, and the next scheduled runs' reports are checked. O7: one manual reconciliation is run and its gated candidates resolved, then the weekly trigger is enabled and a scheduled run observed. The release record names the image and configuration versions and the active generations.
      Leaves out: nothing. Spec §10's deferred decisions stay outside this roadmap.
      ROUTING: writing-plans
